findings.title: The layer rule forbids the imports the planned collector loop and detectors need, and tests/test_layers.py misses relative imports and cannot express 'no program imports another'
findings.evidence: Re-ran f-consistency/layer_rule.py: 'collector imports store FAILS', 'collector imports attribution FAILS', 'analysis imports store FAILS'. tests/test_layers.py:9-18 puts store, collector, attribution, analysis all at layer 2; :43 requires same package or a strictly lower layer. docs/14-baseline-modules.md:304 store.raw 'Imported by: Nothing yet. The collector loop will, in phase 1'; docs/13-build-list.md:17 puts adaptive cadence and overhead guard in component 07 collector.sampler; docs/17-build-prompt.md:269 'the collector loop ... around the existing sampler'. Re-ran g-buildability/layer_rule_cases.py: 'collector imports the raw store, relative: layer test passes; module exit 0'; 'core imports the store package by name: layer test passes'; 'new package server, not in LAYER: ERROR KeyError'; with server/launcher at layer 3, 'server imports the collector: layer test passes'. tests/test_layers.py:23-24 keeps only node.module, so 'from ..cli import app' is invisible (mutation_check: 'layers: core imports cli through a relative import SURVIVED'). docs/17:46 'Five layers ... providers, sampler, attribution, store, analysis' contradicts AGENTS.md:37.
findings.impact: The first phase-1 task that wires the loop where docs/13, 14 and 17 place it turns pytest red, and each builder will invent a different home for the loop. Relative imports and program-to-program imports pass silently, so the boundary that keeps the collector replaceable (docs/17:56) has no test.
findings.proposed_change: docs/14 (figure, store.raw and store.query 'Imported by') and docs/17:46: the running loops live in a new layer-3 package beside cli (e.g. `daemon` or `programs.collector/.server/.launcher`); collector, attribution, store and analysis stay libraries. tests/test_layers.py: add the new package(s) to LAYER; resolve ImportFrom.level > 0 against the module's package; expand `from submeter import x`; add a PROGRAMS set and a test that no program package imports another. Propose the matching AGENTS.md:37 wording to the owner.
findings.cost: About 25 lines in tests/test_layers.py, about ten lines across docs 14 and 17, one proposed line in AGENTS.md
findings.decision_question: Where do the collector loop and server wiring live? (a) new layer-3 program package(s) beside cli, (b) raise collector to layer 3, (c) order the layer-2 packages. Recommend (a): the four libraries stay independent and the program boundary becomes testable.
findings.verification: Re-ran both probes; output matches the saved .out.txt line for line. Re-read tests/test_layers.py:9-43. Tried to refute by finding a doc that places the loop above layer 2: none in docs/13, 14, 17 or prompts/01; AGENTS.md:37 only says 'Add a new package to its LAYER table'. growth.py docstring says detectors choose the tier, so analysis->store is a real planned edge. Nothing is broken today (baseline uses absolute imports only). Merged three leads; E#13's relative-import fix belongs here.

findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:46 'No new dependency without my approval. findings.impact: P4 to P6 tasks stall mid-wave for dependency approval or break AGENTS.md:46. A dashboard that loads uPlot from a CDN, or FastAPI's default /docs page, makes the browser fetch from a third-party host, against fixed rule 3.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13 'Alongside the code' and docs/17:38-39: list the runtime dependencies version 1 expects for owner approval at planning, and add 'All dashboard assets, including the chart library and fonts, ship in the package and are served by the server; the page requests nothing from another host. Hand-write the MCP stdio server? Add tzdata for Windows? findings.verification: Re-read AGENTS.md:46, pyproject.toml, docs/17:38-39, 13:63; grepped uv.lock and docs. Re-fetched the FastAPI page and confirmed both quoted sentences. Considered whether docs/17:38 naming FastAPI counts as the owner's approval: docs/README.md:72-75 ranks 17 last and gives no dependency list, so the conflict with AGENTS.md:46 stands. findings.title: The 20 baseline tests catch 1 of 29 deliberately broken behaviours
findings.evidence: Re-ran e-baseline/mutation_check.py (with PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--basetemp in a temporary folder so it could not collide with other pytest runs): output identical to the saved file. 'unchanged copy: 20 passed'; control caught; only 'a jump of the monotonic clock is no longer a gap' caught; '28 of 29 broken behaviours survived'. Survivors include I/O reported as running total, rule priority ignored, a rule beating kernel-group membership, workload memory not summed, CPU pending at exit and at rollover thrown away, no keyframe after the first, WAL off, histograms not time-weighted, every bucket well covered, an I/O-restricted process dropped, idle counted as busy, config layers reversed, a default and a range differing from docs/08, minute retention ignored, every weekly file expired.
findings.impact: AGENTS.md:45 'A change in behaviour starts with a failing test' has nothing to start from for most promises in docs/14, so parallel builders can break attribution, raw-store and rollup behaviour that sets the numbers with no gate failing.
findings.proposed_change: tests/: a planned task adding focused tests for the survivors (about ten tests: sampler I/O delta, rule priority and kernel-group precedence, aggregate sums, raw exit/rollover/keyframe/WAL, rollup weighting and coverage, provider restricted-I/O and idle, config precedence and docs/08 defaults/ranges, choose_tier and expired_minute). The relative-import part of the layer test is in B1.
findings.cost: About ten tests as one planned task
findings.verification: Reproduced the run exactly. Checked the mutants are not equivalent (each changes an observable output for some input). Caveat added: the 29 mutants were chosen to target behaviours the reviewer suspected were untested, so '1 of 29' describes that sample, not a coverage percentage; docs/14:383 is right that exact sums, rollup totals and the histogram bound are tested directly.

findings.title: Settings validation accepts unknown alert metrics, misspelt thresholds, unselected bad profiles, negative, zero or NaN retention, and crashes on missing or UTF-16 files
findings.evidence: Re-ran e-baseline/config_cases.py: "metric 'cpu_coress' ... accepted", "'commit_fraction' on workload 'browser': accepted", 'verdict.thresholds.cpu_tyme = 0.85: accepted', 'bad values in a profile, no profile selected: accepted', 'profile = 5, profile selected: CRASH TypeError', 'raw = -5 / nan / disk_budget = -1 / min_slope = -1 / cooldown = -60 / unattributed_alert = "250%": accepted', 'UTF-16 ... CRASH UnicodeDecodeError'. New probe verify-8/settings_holes.py: at 00:00:10 UTC 'raw = -5 ... expired_raw -> [2026-11-20.db]', 'raw = 0 ... expired_raw -> [2026-11-20.db]', 'raw = nan ... expired_raw -> []'; 'config check MISSING: exit 1, exception FileNotFoundError'; 'config show MISSING: exit 0'. Code: config.py:153 metric: str; :143 thresholds: dict[str, float]; units.py:137-140 Duration/Size/Rate/Fraction have no range; cli.py:47 silently ignores a named --file that does not exist; cli.py:125 calls load_settings without catching OSError. Docs: 08:130 'A rule that names any other metric is refused when the settings are loaded'; 14:173 'Unknown keys are errors'; AGENTS.md:42.
findings.impact: A typo in an alert or threshold silently does nothing; a bad laptop profile passes config check and fails at run time; retention.raw of 0 or less lets expired_raw list yesterday's raw file right after midnight, before the hourly rollup reads it, and NaN means raw files never expire by age.
findings.proposed_change: core/config.py: AlertRule.metric as a Literal of the seven ids in docs/08:134-140 with the applies-to check (machine / submeter); Verdict.thresholds as a model of named fields; validate every profile at load; finite ranges for every Duration, Size, Rate and Fraction, with retention.raw at least 24h (docs/17:141 floor) and unattributed_alert 0 to 100%. docs/08 'Other settings': add a range column. cli.py: a named --file or --rules that is missing, undecodable or invalid exits 2 with one line per problem. Tests first for each.
findings.cost: About 40 lines of code, a range column in docs/08, two tests
findings.verification: Re-ran config_cases.py (matches the saved output) and wrote settings_holes.py to test the retention consequence and the CLI path directly. Refinement: the lead's 'non-negative' fix is not enough, since retention.raw = 0 also expires yesterday's file at 00:00:10; a floor is needed. Partly a spec gap: docs/08's 'Other settings' table gives no ranges, which is why nothing refuses them. R18 made alert rules structured but its fix ('validated like every other setting') is not met for metric names.

findings.title: The AGENTS.md checks do not type-check Windows-only code on Linux, and ruff format --check also checks Markdown
findings.evidence: New probe verify-8/tooling_gate.py: a win32-guarded wrong return type gives 'as run here: exit 0; Success' and '--platform win32: exit 1; Found 1 error'; a folder holding only note.md with an unformatted Python block gives 'ruff format --check: exit 1; 1 file would be reformatted' (ruff 0.17.6). AGENTS.md:29 lists only 'uv run mypy src tests', while docs/14:11 says mypy was 'checked as Linux and again as Windows'. ground/ruff-format.txt '51 files already formatted' includes Markdown.
findings.impact: Windows-only providers and the launcher written on Linux pass the local gate and fail only in Windows CI; a brief edit with an unformatted Python block fails the format gate, and running the fixer rewrites the brief.
findings.proposed_change: AGENTS.md Checks (owner approval): add 'uv run mypy --platform win32 src tests' and 'uv run mypy --platform linux src tests'. pyproject.toml [tool.ruff]: extend-exclude = ['*.md'] (or exclude docs/ from format).
findings.verification: Wrote and ran my own probe in a temporary folder; both behaviours reproduced. Nothing fails today (lead ran mypy --platform win32 clean), so this is a gate gap, low.

findings.title: The run file's life is contradictory: written only at the end yet needed while live, 'until read' yet needed for re-attach, two candidate writers of final totals, and no deleter
findings.evidence: docs/17:66 the launcher 'writes the group's totals to its run file when the command ends'; 17:68 'The collector finds live groups from the run files ... After a restart it re-attaches to every live group'; 17:67 'a small detached holder, or the collector. Choose one and test it'; R15 (docs/16:147) settled 'held open by a detached helper'; AGENTS.md:43 and docs/05:52 make the launcher the only writer of run files; docs/06:17 runs/*.json 'Kept for: Until read'; docs/05:44 'registers the group with the collector' although the collector has no API; store/files.py:26 Program = Literal['collector', 'server'] and files.py has runs_dir but no expiry for it.
findings.impact: A run file written only at exit cannot tell a restarted collector which groups are live, and deleting on 'read' can remove it before final totals land, so a run's exact cost (job 1, P2 gate 'its final totals survive its exit') is lost or written twice.
findings.proposed_change: docs/06 runs row, docs/17:66-68 and :107, docs/05:44: 'The launcher writes the run file when the group is created (state live) and replaces it by atomic rename with final totals when the group empties (state final). When the command leaves processes behind, a detached copy of the launcher holds the group and writes the final state; the collector never writes it. The server copies a final run file into history's run table and then deletes it.' Delete 'or the collector' from 17:67.
findings.verification: Re-read every cited line. Refutation attempt: docs/README.md:75 makes the topic files (incl. 16) win over 17, so R15's detached helper already decides the holder question; the 'or the collector' in 17:67 is a defect, not an open decision, and needs_decision drops to false. The live/final timing, the 'until read' lifetime and the missing deleter are not settled anywhere. Overlaps G-buildability#8 items 2-3 (cluster B16), kept here.

findings.title: The 13 API routes cover neither cost nor runs, the state-changing commands have no route or writer, and R05's ingest route is missing
findings.evidence: docs/13:71-83 lists health, capabilities, config, epochs, workloads, workloads/{id}/processes, series, verdict, findings, diff, sessions GET/POST, WS live; none returns session_summary or run rows. docs/13:59 'cost cost per workload, session or run'; R26 (16:219) 'cost and diff read the summaries'. docs/05:50 and the 05 figure route the CLI through the API, while docs/17:46 calls the CLI a thin reader 'over store and analysis'. docs/13:64 'config ... reload | rotate-token' and :66 'store ... backup' act on server-owned files (06:16 backups, 06:20 token), yet 13:82 and 17:254 allow no write but session markers. R05 (16:81) 'The ingest API accepts a second collector'; 17:79 'Design the ingest path'; no route.
findings.impact: If the CLI goes through the API as 05:50 says, `cost`, `report`, `export` and `store status` have nothing to call; `config rotate-token` and `store backup` can work only by the CLI writing server-owned files (a second writer) or through an unstated channel; phase 7 has no ingest path.
findings.proposed_change: docs/05:50 and 17:46: say which commands read store files directly and which call the API. docs/13 routes and 17:254: add GET /cost and GET /runs if the CLI goes through the API; state that session start and stop are both markers on POST /sessions; add local admin routes (POST /config/reload, /token/rotate, /backups) or name the file channel (see B15); reserve an ingest route for phase 7 or mark R05's ingest out of version 1. Update the count in 13:5 and README.
findings.verification: Re-read all lines. Partly refuted: 'session markers' (13:30) is plural, so POST /sessions can carry stop as well as start; and MCP lives inside the server (17:53), so the P6 'own cost' gate does not need an HTTP route. The root defect is 05:50 vs 17:46 on whether the CLI reads through the API, plus the write commands with no writer and R05's missing route (R05's fix is not reflected in the route list, so it is not rejected as already covered). Overlaps B15 on reload and rotate-token.

findings.title: Behaviours named once and never specified: profile selection, quiet_hours format, dashboard token delivery, unended sessions, group membership, kernel totals versus polled sums, the System bucket
findings.evidence: Profile: docs/08:117 'Each machine can carry a named profile' is the only spec; config.py:280 profile= is the only selector, cli.py:111 offers --profile on config show only, config.py:267 skips SUBMETER_PROFILE (config_cases: 'SUBMETER_PROFILE=laptop in the environment: accepted (1 keys set)', the file's key only). quiet_hours: docs/08:98 only; config.py:173 str | None, unvalidated. Token: docs/17:148 token on every HTTP and WS request; no doc says how the browser page obtains it (grep 'token'). Sessions: docs/04:23 and 06:74 'summarised when they end'; grep for unended or overlapping sessions finds nothing. Membership: rules.py:133 takes a `tagged` map; no doc says how the collector learns it. Kernel vs polled: rules.py:213-216 labels a kernel workload KERNEL while :204-211 sum polled processes (attribution_cases section 3: 'source=kernel, cpu_s=0.4: the label says kernel, the figure is the polled sum'). System: docs/02:141 'Kernel time, interrupts, deferred calls'; rules.py:36 SYSTEM is never produced (doc_vs_code section 5: "a 'system' row is produced: False").
findings.impact: Each is a guess for a builder. The last three decide whether job 1's tagged figures are the kernel's and whether the 2% reconciliation check can fail at all.
findings.proposed_change: One sentence each: docs/08 'How configuration behaves' names the profile selector (SUBMETER_PROFILE, else none); docs/08 Alerts gives quiet_hours as "HH:MM-HH:MM" local time, validated; docs/06 or 17 says how the dashboard gets the token (e.g. a `submeter open` one-time code exchanged for an HttpOnly cookie); docs/04 or 06: a session with no stop is closed at its last covered sample and summarised then, sessions may overlap; docs/05: membership from /proc/PID/cgroup and the job's process list, and a tagged workload's totals are the group's kernel deltas, polled processes feeding only the tree view; docs/02 and 17: define System from counters and report the remainder separately.
findings.verification: Grepped docs/ (excluding 16) for profile, quiet, token, session end/overlap, membership and System; each appears only at the cited lines. Re-read rules.py:125-233. Corrected a citation: the System text is docs/02:141, not 02:173 (the file has 158 lines). The System derivation likely also sits in a measurement-lens cluster; kept here only as the spec gap.

findings.title: docs/17 adds requirements the topic files lack and drops others, so the compact spec and the topic files describe different builds
findings.evidence: grep of docs 01-16 finds no hit for: '150 MB' (17:230), 'synchronous' (17:138), 'idempotent' or 'final 30 seconds' (17:123), 'breakaway' or 'kill-on-close' (17:69), every data file restricted (17:146; 06:20 restricts only the token), 'previous version' (17:140), 'working director(y/ies)' withheld from MCP (17:148; 08:125 says command lines only), 'workload level' growth (17:154). 17:96 'parent chain' vs 08:217 and 14:261 'parent, the program that started the process' and rules.py _direct(process, groups, parent) using the immediate parent. 17:148 'check Origin on the WebSocket' vs 15:25 P4 gate 'requests ... with a foreign Origin are refused' and 13:30. Dropped from 17: known limits 17:218-226 omit docs/10's VRAM (10:13) and Restricted (10:16) rows; 17:274 P6 gate omits 'own cost' (15:33); 17:275 phase 7 has no gate (15:37); 17:212 omits the settings view (13:31); 17:94 order omits Submeter itself (14:259).
findings.impact: docs/README.md:75 says the topic file wins where they differ, and prompts/README says 17 can start a single-session build alone: a builder from 17 checks Origin only on the WebSocket and fails the P4 gate, or builds parent-chain matching the code lacks; a plan from the topic files loses the memory budget, breakaway rule and file permissions.

Copy the missing limits and gates into 17.
findings.verification: Ran my own greps over docs 01-16 for each 17-only item (no hits except 06:20 and 16:243 for the token), read docs/10 rows against 17:218-226, and read 17:94, 212, 274-275. R04's fix (16:75) says the API 'checks Host and Origin headers' without limiting it to the WebSocket, so 17:148 is the narrow statement. findings.title: Wording slips that do not change a stored number, one of which makes a Windows suspend check unable to fail
findings.evidence: 'Both programs' at docs/15:46, 17:148, 17:264 against three programs (13:5). docs/06:20 'one lock per program' while many launchers run; files.py:26 Program = collector | server. docs/03:33 'cpu time 91% of capacity' vs 03:43-44 reconciled busy 88+1+3+1 = 93 (100 - idle 7). 16:107 and 17:77 'parent started before the child' vs 14:260 'no later than' and rules.py:146 (equal start times allowed). docs/03:5 'Every command also takes --json' vs cli.py:108-130 (config show/check have none). 17:254 '/api/v1' prefix vs 13:71-83 none. docs/14:173 'Unknown keys are errors' vs config.py:143 thresholds dict (cpu_tyme accepted). docs/reference/windows-priorities.md:70 checks suspend with `top --seconds 60`, but sampler.py:39 gap_after_s = 30.0 makes any interval over 30 s a gap (cli_cases: 'top --seconds 31: ... CPU-seconds summed over all workloads=0.000').
findings.impact: Small misreadings for builders; the windows-priorities suspend check passes whether or not suspend is handled, and the 'started before' wording would lead a test author to reject equal start times that the code correctly accepts.
findings.proposed_change: One-line edits: 'every program' in 15 and 17; locks only for collector and server; 03:33 '93%'; 'no later than' in 16 and 17; mark config show/check --json as not yet in the baseline; one route prefix in 13 and 17; qualify 14:173 for verdict.thresholds (or fix it with B4); windows-priorities.md:70 uses an interval under 30 s across the sleep and checks the gap flag.
findings.verification: Re-read each pair of locations, the sampler gap rule and cli.py. Spot-checked the arithmetic (93 not 91). Item 12 (suspend check) has a real effect on a Windows verification step, but it is a reference-doc fix, so the cluster stays low.

findings.title: Several gates need data, hardware or the owner's machine that nothing provides, and some lack a reference or pass criterion
findings.evidence: docs/15:9 P0 '`doctor` is correct on both' has no reference; 'Per-process VRAM is checked against the adapter total' needs a GPU; 'over a working day' (15:45) is the owner's day. 17:269 'I will run a 24-hour soak myself' has no pass criterion. 15:21 P3 slow leak needs a multi-day hourly fixture (17:155 'at least 7 days'); '`why` answers in under 2 seconds' names no data volume or machine. 15:25 P4 '30-day range loads in under 1 second' needs 30 days of minute and hourly files that nothing generates. 15:37 P7 needs WSL2: re-fetched https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/howto/run-workflows-azure/: 'GitHub runners, however, run as a service.' 'This means that they are not on a user session, hence they cannot run WSL (or any other store application).'
findings.impact: Builders and checkers would each invent the reference data and procedure, so a gate pass would mean different things in different sessions, and owner-run gates have no written steps.
findings.proposed_change: docs/PLAN.md gates section (prompts/01 stage 2 item 6) must, per gate: name the reference (P0 doctor: a committed expected matrix per runner; on the owner's machine the owner confirms against probe output), the data (synthetic 3-hour raw fixture for the hourly 0.1% check; synthetic 7-day and 30-day stores for P3 and P4), the machine (VRAM, WSL share and P7 are owner procedures), and numeric criteria for the 24-hour soak (overhead, collector memory growth, integrity_check ok, gaps only where recorded). docs/15 and 17:268-274 then restate those references in one line each.
findings.cost: About 30 lines in PLAN.md, a few lines in docs 15 and 17
findings.verification: Re-read 15:9-37 and 17:266-275; re-fetched the Ubuntu WSL page and confirmed the quote. Downgraded high to medium and fix now to plan: prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:84 already requires, per gate, 'the exact commands or procedure, the pass criteria as numbers, the evidence to keep, who checks it ... and which gates need me or a second operating system', so writing procedures is stage-2 work by design and no gate fails at run time. Refuted two sub-claims: (1) the hourly 0.1% check can be done in a 30-minute soak that straddles an hour boundary, since the bucket is final 30 s after it ends (17:123), or from a synthetic fixture; (2) the P0 VRAM check needs a probe and a GPU, not component 23.

findings.title: Hosted CI runners are elevated, GPU-less and sessionless, so they cannot stand in for the owner's unprivileged machine
findings.evidence: Re-fetched https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners: 'Windows virtual machines are configured to run as administrators with User Account Control (UAC) disabled.'; 'The Linux and macOS virtual machines both run using passwordless sudo.'; standard public-repo rows Linux and Windows '4 CPU, 16 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD'; GPU only under larger runners. Ubuntu WSL page: 'GitHub runners, however, run as a service ... cannot run WSL'. docs/17:266 'Set up CI on Windows and Linux runners in phase 0, because you can only run one OS yourself'; docs/15:9 P0 '`doctor` is correct on both'; 15:13 P1 '30-minute CI soak stays inside the budget' while 17:230 defines the budget 'With 300 processes running'. No .github folder exists.
findings.impact: On the Windows runner every process is readable, so Restricted handling, OpenProcess failures, the token-file ACL and any accidental need for elevation (fixed rule 2) pass in CI; doctor there reports an administrator's matrix; the P1 soak runs at an unknown process count; logon task, notifications, WSL2 and GPU cannot run there.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15 (P0) and docs/17:266: 'CI proves portability: ruff, mypy (with --platform for the other OS), pytest, fixture parsing and logic on both OSes. It does not prove privilege, hardware or session behaviour, because Windows runners are administrators with UAC off. Tests that need an unprivileged user, a user session (logon task, notifications, WSL) or hardware (GPU, battery, suspend) are marked and run on the owner's machine at the gate. The CI soak states its process count.' Run CI on every pushed branch from wave 1.
findings.cost: A paragraph in docs 15 and 17; the CI workflow is a P0 task
findings.verification: Re-fetched both vendor pages; all quoted sentences are present. Downgraded high to medium: prompts/01:3 puts the build session on the owner's Windows 11 work computer, so unprivileged Windows behaviour can be tested locally, and the elevated runner is a usable source for the 'with elevation' column docs/17:268 asks for. The remaining risk is that gate wording names CI as the proof (15:9, 15:13). The claim that the Ubuntu runner lacks a user systemd session for cgroup delegation (component 13/14 Linux half) was not verified here; would be settled by a CI job running `systemctl --user is-system-running; systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes true`.

findings.title: Phase gates depend on components of later phases
findings.evidence: P1 gate 'totals reconcile within 2%' (15:13) needs 'the four fixed buckets, reconciliation check', component 15 in P2 (13:25); baseline aggregate() produces no system row (f-consistency/doc_vs_code section 5: "a 'system' row is produced: False"). P1 asks for 'the minute and history files ..., retention and backups' (17:269), but no component is the server process: server.api is component 20 in P4 (13:30) and docs/14:84 lists 'the server' as not built. P2 'A session's cost reads the same before and after its raw data is deleted' (15:17) needs session markers, whose only route is POST /sessions (13:82, P4) while only the server writes history (AGENTS.md:43). P0 'The cost of one full sample is measured' (15:9) with only psutil built (bulk providers are components 04/05 in P1); docs/11:19 'One full sample of 300 processes takes more than 10 ms in phase 0' is the Rust trigger, and the psutil provider measured 111.2 ms median at 447 processes on this Linux machine (probes/measure/snapshot_cost.out.txt). P7 'moves to directly after phase 2' (15:37) but R05's ingest route is in no list (13:70-83).
findings.impact: Builders either pull later components forward untracked or fail the gate; the Rust decision would be taken on the fallback provider the brief already expects to miss the target.
findings.proposed_change: docs/15 and docs/13: (a) P0 times a minimal bulk-snapshot prototype (or the measurement moves to the P1 gate) and says which provider is timed; (b) move the reconciliation part of component 15 to P1; (c) add a 'server' program component in P1 (rollups, retention, backups, integrity check, run-file ingestion, epochs); (d) say whether CLI commands read store files directly, and give sessions a P2 path; (e) P7 names its ingest route and moves with it.
findings.decision_question: Do CLI commands read store files directly (API serves dashboard and MCP only), or go through the API, which pulls a minimal API into P2? Recommend direct reads: reading breaks no one-writer rule and keeps P2 and P3 independent of P4.
findings.verification: Re-read 13:11-35, 15:9-37, 17:268-275, docs/11:17-21 and docs/14:80-84; confirmed the system-row result and the snapshot figure in saved outputs (not re-timed). Downgraded high to medium: no gate fails at run time; the dependency graph prompts/01:83 (stage 2 item 5) asks for would expose these, and the phase order is open to challenge (prompts/01:19). The ingest-route part overlaps B8.

findings.title: No stated channel carries stop, a session's interval override or session start to the collector, and Windows has no signal for a graceful stop
findings.evidence: docs/05:5 'Three programs share nothing but files on disk'; 17:56 'None of the three imports another'; the collector has no API. Needing a channel: `daemon stop` (13:55); 'A session may override the sampling interval for its own duration' (17:190; 08:74 `session start bench --interval 250ms`) while sessions are written by the server (POST /sessions, 13:82; history.db, 06:15); the launcher 'registers the group with the collector' (05:44) while the run file is written 'when the command ends' (17:66). Re-fetched https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html (os.kill): 'Windows: The signal.CTRL_C_EVENT and signal.CTRL_BREAK_EVENT signals are special signals which can only be sent to console processes which share a common console window, e.g., some subprocesses. Any other value for sig will cause the process to be unconditionally killed by the TerminateProcess API, and the exit code will be set to sig.'
findings.impact: On Windows, `daemon stop` can only kill the collector and server (bounded by the 5-second loss rule, 17:138, but never a clean shutdown); a session's interval override and session boundaries have no path to the collector; parallel builders would each invent a mechanism.
findings.proposed_change: docs/05 and docs/06: name files as the only channel and list them, e.g. under state/control/: `stop-<program>` (removed by the program on exit), `sessions/<id>.json` written by whoever starts or stops the session and read by the collector each tick, `runs/<id>.json` written live at launch (see B7); config reload by settings-file mtime. Collector reports (overhead guard, provider status) go as `event` rows in its raw file, which the server turns into findings or epochs.
findings.cost: A table of about 5 rows in docs 06 and a paragraph in docs 05
findings.decision_question: Commands reach the programs through files polled each tick, or through a loopback control endpoint on the collector (a second port and token)? Recommend files: no new listener, same on both OSes, survive restarts, keep the collector replaceable.
findings.verification: Re-read every cited line (daemon stop is 13:55, not 13:58) and re-fetched the os.kill paragraph. Downgraded high to medium and narrowed: files are already the stated channel (05:5); 'Hot reload ... on file change' (17:187) gives config reload a path through the settings file; and 17:130 'The collector records such events in the raw file and the server turns them into epochs' with the raw `event` table (13:39, raw.py:35) already carries collector-to-server events, so the overhead-guard finding has a path. What is left unspecified is stop on Windows, the session-to-collector path and run-file registration.

findings.title: Builders would have to guess the shared interfaces: minute and history table columns, the WS /live messages, the --json shapes and the MCP transport
findings.evidence: Columns exist only for the 8 raw tables (store/raw.py:34-53). The minute file (meta, rollup_1m) and history file (meta, workload, epoch, rollup_1h, exe_1h, run, session, session_summary, finding, baseline; docs/13:40-41) have no columns anywhere (grep for CREATE TABLE and the table names: only 05:75-77, 13:40-41, 17:251-252). 'WS /live' (13:83) has no message format, rate or handshake. 'every command accepts --json with a stable schema' (17:197) has no schema; baseline shapes differ: doctor an object with 'version' (cli.py:68), top a bare list (cli.py:96), store status {'bytes','total'} (cli.py:138); config show/check have no --json. 17:53 puts MCP inside the server; 15:33 'its own cost' does not say how a request identifies its run. 17:187 'Settings that need a restart must say so' with no list.
findings.impact: Parallel builders of the server writers, detectors, API and CLI would define the shared contract differently and meet only at integration.
findings.proposed_change: Planned first P1 task with one owner: the DDL of the 12 minute and history tables in docs/06 (rollup tables mapping to Bucket). Doc paragraphs: a short WS /live message schema and token handshake in docs/13; a JSON envelope {"schema": "submeter.<command>/1", ...} in docs/03 with a snapshot test per command; MCP transport choice and how 'own' run is identified (e.g. SUBMETER_RUN set by the launcher) in docs/17:53; the restart-only settings in docs/08.
findings.cost: DDL as a planned task; a paragraph each in docs 03, 08, 13, 17; under 50 lines for the JSON envelope
findings.verification: Re-read raw.py:30-53, cli.py:55-142, docs/13:37-83; grepped docs and src for schema text. Changed disposition from fix now to plan because the main item (12 tables of DDL) exceeds a small doc change. The run-file items (lead's 2 and 3) are kept in B7. The MCP spec quotes were not re-fetched (medium finding); the transport point rests on 17:53 alone.

findings.title: The load generator, fixture recorder, synthetic multi-day stores and CI have no phase, and the synthetic store generator is named nowhere
findings.evidence: docs/13:43-51 'Alongside the code' lists CI, recorded fixtures and a load generator without phases or component numbers. R19's fix (16:171) 'A load generator ships with the tests'; g-buildability/shared_files.out.txt: 'folders under tests/ (fixtures, load generator): none', '.github folder present: False'. prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:91 'each of the 25 components is in a task or cut by a ruling'. No doc names a generator of multi-day raw, minute and history files, which the P3 slow-leak fixture (17:155, 7 days) and the P4 30-day range (15:25) need.
findings.impact: The plan's component check can pass with no task for the tools the P1 to P4 gates depend on; the multi-day store generator may be discovered only at the P4 gate.
findings.proposed_change: docs/13: give each 'Alongside the code' item a phase (CI and load generator P0; provider recorder and synthetic store generator P1) and add the synthetic store generator to the list; prompts/01:91 counts them with the components.
findings.cost: Four table rows or list lines and one number in prompts/01
findings.verification: Re-read 13:43-51, 16:171 and prompts/01. Downgraded medium to low: prompts/01:85 (item 7) already requires a test strategy covering 'fixtures, the load generator, recorded provider output, the CI matrix', and :87 (item 9) says 'Nothing in the brief is left without a task or an explicit not in version 1', so the load generator and CI are already forced into the plan; only the synthetic multi-day store is genuinely unnamed. The lead cited prompts/01:99; the line is 91.

findings.title: Every figure this review measured comes from Linux; the plan's Windows decisions need figures from the owner's machine
findings.evidence: docs/review/ground/platform-check.txt line 1: 'Linux-7.0.0-43-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 | Python 3.14.5 | psutil 7.2.2'; line 2 'administrator or root: False'. probes/measure/snapshot_cost.out.txt: '447 processes: wall median 111.2 ms' (psutil) and '448 processes: wall median 11.2 ms' (/proc). docs/11:19 Rust trigger at 10 ms per full sample in phase 0. prompts/01:3 assumes the session runs on the Windows 11 work computer; CI Windows runners are administrators (B13).
findings.impact: The Rust-or-Python decision, the overhead budget, the Restricted share and every Windows claim in docs/09 rest on numbers no one has taken on the target; if the plan's risk register (prompts/01 stage 2 item 8) uses these Linux figures, those decisions are made on the wrong OS.
findings.proposed_change: docs/PLAN.md marks every figure that came from Linux. Before the Rust decision, run on the owner's Windows machine as the signed-in user, saved under docs/review/ground-windows/: the four checks, platform_check.py, a bulk-snapshot prototype timed over 20 runs with the process count, a nested Job Object with accounting read after children exit, and the Restricted count and its CPU share.
findings.cost: One owner-machine session of probes; a paragraph in PLAN.md
findings.verification: Re-read the ground and measure outputs (not re-timed). Downgraded medium to low: this is a caveat on the review's evidence rather than a defect in the brief. prompts/01:28-29 already has the session run the checks and platform_check.py on the Windows machine, docs/reference/windows-priorities.md lists the Windows checks, and docs/17:56 puts the Rust measurement in phase 0 on the target. The report's 'Not checked' section and PLAN.md must say the figures are Linux-only.
